wording_constraint: This is a rule-based status computed from the frozen model's own inputs and rollout against a fixed reference distribution. It is NOT a calibrated probability, NOT a confidence score and NOT a probability of correctness. No reliability estimator was fitted and no held-out test label was used to set any threshold.

input_scaler.consequence: X_train/X_val/X_test.npy are ALREADY standardized by this scaler, so a stored value IS a z-score against the reference train distribution. Input-OOD indicators therefore need no new fit and no new scaler — the crucial precondition for computing them without training.

results/long_horizon_rollout/latent_stab.content: per-sample per-step latent norm / delta / cosine, K=0..10

results/long_horizon_rollout/latent_cont.content: observed contraction ratios and per-sample verdicts

results/long_horizon_rollout/probability.content: per-sample probability drift, range, oscillation, saturation

results/long_horizon_rollout/forecast_er.content: AGGREGATE state MAE/RMSE by horizon vs persistence and train-mean

results/long_horizon_rollout/horizon_sta.content: pre-declared numerical stability rules, STABLE at every K=1..10

computable_without_training: input OOD: the arrays are already in frozen-scaler z units
rollout stability: latent norms and step deltas are arithmetic on the frozen model's own output
forecast self-consistency: differences between successive predicted states and probabilities
analytic latent-norm bounds: closed form from the frozen LayerNorm and Linear weights
retrospective forecast error: Y_multistep_test.npy holds the observed future state in the same target_scaler space the decoder outputs — usable AFTER the fact only

deliberately_not_computed.why_not: would require fitting an estimator on labels; the task forbids a new learned model and forbids tuning on test labels. No calibration is claimed.

docs/LONG_HORIZON_ROLLOUT.md section 11: the V4 transition is a DETERMINISTIC point estimate in latent space and does not predict a distribution. There is no variance to read; inventing one from the rollout spread would be a number without a meaning.
requires either new models or stochastic forward passes, i.e. a new component and a non-deterministic output. Both are out of scope for a frozen-model reliability layer.

deliberately_not_computed.metric: latent-norm growth as an instability signal
deliberately_not_computed.why_not: COMPUTED and reported, but weak by construction: the transition terminates in LayerNorm, which bounds the latent RMS. Recorded as architectural, not learned.

reference_flag_rate_note: The train row is the rule's BASE RATE on the very distribution its thresholds came from: an ELEVATED tier is by construction a ~1% event per indicator. The held-out rate is only interpretable against it.

input_shift_margin_justification.ground_a: The condition must not fire on data the reference distribution covers. Margin 0 does (10 val sequences slightly extend the train range, as any finite sample will). The smallest margin in {0, 1, 3, 5} that flags neither train nor val is 1.0 SD, so 3.0 satisfies this with room to spare.
input_shift_margin_justification.ground_b: 3.0 is not a new free parameter: |z| > 3 is already one of this layer's indicators (frac_gt3, per the task specification), so the hard condition reuses the same conventional numerical-outlier threshold.
input_shift_margin_justification.honest_caveat: 3.0 is the more conservative of two defensible values, not the unique value the evidence forces. At 1.0 SD the same rule would flag 21 held-out sequences instead of 11. Both counts are in input_shift_margin_sensitivity.

retrospective_forecast_error.label: retrospective forecast error analysis
retrospective_forecast_error.definition: decoded state at t+k vs OBSERVED state at t+k from Y_multistep_test.npy, in target_scaler space
retrospective_forecast_error.correlation_note: Spearman rho against sequence-mean state MAE over k=1..5. These correlations are REPORTED, not used: no threshold was chosen from them. latent_norm_max correlates NEGATIVELY, which contradicts its 'larger is worse' framing and is recorded as a limitation rather than corrected.

failsafe_self_tests.note: Detector self-tests on deliberately corrupted tensors. These are NOT data examples and appear in no reported statistic or CSV row.

tests.condition: encoder latent norm past analytic bound
rollout latent norm explosion at k=3

frozen_path_agreement.cause: screening_predictions.csv was produced on MPS; the reliability layer pins CPU for determinism. The gap is float32 device arithmetic, not a model change.

known_limitations: The status is rule-based. It is NOT a calibrated probability and no calibration was attempted or established.

The reference distribution is the multiday_benchmark_K5 TRAIN split — the distribution of the scaler the inference path uses. The checkpoint's own training distribution (single-day temporal_benchmark_v2) no longer exists on disk, so this layer measures distance from the scaler's reference, not from the weights' reference. The documented train/eval normalisation mismatch is inherited, not repaired.
One held-out day (Friday-02-03-2018, 3,115 sequences, 3 observable onsets). Every held-out rate is a single-day rate.

Latent-norm stability is largely architectural: the transition ends in LayerNorm, which bounds the latent RMS by construction. H7 is therefore a corruption detector, not an instability detector, and latent_norm_max correlates negatively with retrospective error.
ELEVATED is a ~1% per-indicator event by construction, so the CAUTION rate is a property of the quantile choice as much as of the data.

The retrospective study measures STATE reconstruction error, not attack-label correctness. It shows the layer separates conditions under which the decoder is worse; it does not show the layer predicts label errors.
11 UNRELIABLE sequences is too few to estimate any rate. They are one physical event observed through a sliding 10-window lookback, not 11 independent samples.
No abstention is executed. This layer reports; Task 16 owns the ALERT / BENIGN / ABSTAIN decision.
